additions.note: Hosted flagship for complex professional work, research, and agentic coding. Available at launch in ChatGPT Work and Codex for eligible paid users, and in the OpenAI API as gpt-6.2-astra with optional Ultrafast. Standard API rates are $8 input, $0.40 cached input, and $40 output per million tokens.

Hosted successor to GPT-6.1 Sol for coding and professional work. Available at launch in ChatGPT Work and Codex for eligible paid users, and in the OpenAI API as gpt-6.2-sol with optional Ultrafast. Standard API rates remain $2 input, $0.10 cached input, and $10 output per million tokens.
Hosted audio-driven avatar model that uses reference footage and speech context to generate lip sync and gestures. Available through HeyGen's platform and API at launch.

Full release of the 9B multimodal reasoning model with recurrent layer reuse and up to 512K context. SenseTime published Apache-2.0 checkpoints, including a 4-bit AWQ variant. The Hugging Face model repository requires accepting its access terms.
Hosted multimodal decision models that return structured answers and confidence scores. Both add audio input and five decision tasks and were available through the Liquid API at launch.

Embodied world model for robot control on Huawei Ascend hardware. Huawei introduced the model and announced plans to open-source it at the launch event. Downloadable weights were not verified at the event.
Faster, lower-cost hosted variant of Seedance 2.5. The BytePlus ModelArk endpoint generates clips with audio at 480p or 720p for up to 30 seconds.
Scientific multimodal model for research tasks that combine data interpretation, tool use, and multi-step verification. Shanghai AI Lab published the model weights under the MIT license.

Downloadable full-duplex world model for real-time audio-visual interaction, initialized from MiniMax H3. The Causal Base bundle includes video and audio components and is distributed under the repository's MiniMax H3-derived terms.
Hosted text-to-image variant that generates 360-degree panoramas. The date is the OpenRouter API listing.
Hosted image-generation update with faster generation and improvements to rendered text and fine detail. It replaced the earlier Flash in Recraft Studio and uses recraftv4_1_flash_v2 in the API.
Apache-2.0 downloadable checkpoint for the 594B mixture-of-experts model with 17B active parameters and image input, following the November 5 Tinker release.
Downloadable FP4 prompt expander for text-to-image generation, fine-tuned from Qwen3.8-27B. MiniMax supplied a task prompt for image editing and released model weights for the text-to-image expander.

dateEvidence.result: OpenAI's November 17 announcement confirms both model IDs, launch availability, and standard API pricing.
HeyGen's own November 17 release confirms same-day platform and API access.
The publisher's card dates the full release November 17 and identifies the earlier preview separately. Repository metadata confirms Apache-2.0, listed weight shards, and automatic gating.
Liquid AI's November 16 post announces both models and same-day API access.
The replay and launch notice establish the November 16 unveiling. The event did not establish a public weight download.
BytePlus lists the dated Flash ID as a new ModelArk release, corroborating the reported November 15 API rollout after the November 12 introduction.
Publisher revision 6ba152f dated November 15 UTC contains all 120 shards referenced by its weight index. The technical report followed on November 16.
The November 13 UTC model revision contains 33 weight files. The repository's November 12 creation commit predates the weight upload.
OpenRouter's model page dates its image API listing November 13. The date embedded in the snapshot ID is November 12.
The November 13 changelog and dated update to the launch post confirm the new Studio model and API ID.
Publisher upload-model commit 78cb6c0 dated November 12 UTC establishes the downloadable checkpoint's date.
The first November 10 UTC revision contains four Safetensors files. Later coverage discussed that same checkpoint.

exclusions.candidate: K2 Horizon family; HeyGen Decision 1; Perplexity Decider v1.3
exclusions.reason: The timeline already records the model releases. Recent articles and the K2 Horizon paper cover those existing entries.

exclusions.candidate: Microsoft Aion Instruct November 13 post; DeepSeek app APIs
exclusions.reason: Microsoft dates the standalone Aion Instruct package to October and schedules the Windows Insider rollout for December. DeepSeek documents newly exposed app APIs without identifying a new model checkpoint.
